stories.title: Salesforce Acquires Cresta for $2.7B, Adding Voice Agents to Complete Its CX Stack After Fin
stories.body: On November 2, 2026, Salesforce signed a definitive agreement to acquire voice AI company Cresta for a reported $2.7 billion, following its earlier $3.6 billion acquisition of Fin (formerly Intercom) in June 2026. Cresta's voice agents are already deployed at enterprise scale with brands including Marriott, Comcast, Alaska Airlines, and United Airlines. Combined with Fin's text-first chat engine, Salesforce now owns both a text-first and a voice-first service agent, spending more than $6 billion on customer-service AI in a single year.
stories.why: Two of the named competitors in our competitive landscape — Cresta and Fin — are now inside Salesforce's platform, raising the consolidation stakes and shifting the buy-vs-build calculus for any enterprise retailer evaluating standalone agents. Sellers should proactively address how Graas competes with or complements a Salesforce-bundled stack, particularly for retailers already running Service Cloud.

stories.title: Gartner Names 'Context Graphs' Essential Infrastructure for AI Agents — 42% Say Agent Costs Now Exceed Value Realized
stories.body: In a September 2026 report ('Context Graphs Ground AI Agents With Enterprise Knowledge'), Gartner identifies context graphs as the foundational layer that grounds AI agents in declarative, procedural, and causal knowledge required to reason about enterprise tasks, with policies enforced through runtime constraints. Gartner's data shows 42% of enterprises now report AI agent costs exceed value realized, and only 6% report meaningful ROI from AI. By 2028, Gartner predicts over 50% of AI agent systems will rely on context graphs.
stories.why: This is the single most direct analyst validation of the architecture argument Graas makes on every call: agents fail without a governed context layer beneath them, and the majority of enterprise AI spend is not yet returning value. Cite the 42% 'costs exceed value' figure as the reason pilots stall, then position Graas's context layer as the fix.

stories.title: BCG: 59% of CPG Companies Have No Meaningful Agentic AI Capabilities as AI-Driven Traffic Races Toward Organic Search Parity
stories.body: A BCG GenAI CPG Survey published October 30, 2026, finds that while 80% of US consumers use AI and nearly half shop with it, 59% of CPG companies report no meaningful agentic AI capabilities today. AI-driven referrals currently account for less than 1% of website visits but could reach 5% by end of 2026, with BCG projecting AI-driven traffic will overtake organic search in the US as early as 2028. BCG's survey of 150 retailers and brands also found 87% never share customer data with AI agents — a structural data-access blocker for any agent deployment.
stories.why: This is a named BCG report with a release date in the last 30 days and hard adoption-gap numbers that reframe urgency for CPG prospects: the window to build agent infrastructure before AI-driven traffic displaces organic search is measured in months, not years. The 87% data-sharing figure is a direct conversation starter about why agents stall — no data access, no agent performance.

stories.title: Tredence Agentic AI Recovers $6.5M in Trade Deductions for Enterprise CPG Client Across 30+ Integrated Systems
stories.body: Tredence's agentic AI deduction-management solution, integrated across 30+ systems including SAP, EDI, retailer portals, and email, automatically evaluates each trade deduction, assigns reason codes, and recommends next-best actions — recovering $6.5M from roughly $40M in addressable deduction spend for one unnamed enterprise CPG client. The case illustrates a live back-office workflow where an agent replaces manual exception handling rather than a pilot chatbot. Retailers deploying agents across supply chain and back-office operations are seeing measurable returns in faster decisions and lower cost to serve.
stories.why: This is a verifiable outcome number attached to a real CPG workflow — exactly the proof-point a Graas seller needs when a prospect says 'show me where agents work in our world.' Trade deduction management is a universal CPG pain point, making this directly transferable to distributor and CPG accounts in any region.

stories.title: Decagon Named Gartner Cool Vendor, Launches Experiment Hub and Personal Agent Consent Protocol in October 2026
stories.body: Decagon was named a Gartner Cool Vendor in the 2026 Coolest Vendor Innovations in CRM report, and in October launched two new products: Experiment Hub (October 22), an experimentation platform for testing agent behavior, and the Personal Agent Consent & Trust Protocol — PACT (October 6), designed to govern how AI agents interact on behalf of consumers. The company also announced a partnership with OpenAI on its new B2B marketplace (October 2) and separately partners with Databricks to bring enterprise context into every customer conversation. Decagon now sits at a $4.5 billion valuation with 100+ enterprise customers following its January 2026 $250M Series D.
stories.why: Decagon is a direct competitor and is moving fast on both product and enterprise data infrastructure — the Databricks context partnership is a direct play on the same data-grounding problem Graas solves. Sellers need to know Decagon's current differentiation and positioning so they can articulate where Graas's context layer approach is structurally different.
